question: Around the _______ th century BCE, Mahāpadma Nanda rose to prominence in Magadha.
solution:
The correct answer is __**5th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mahāpadma Nanda** was the founder of the Nanda Dynasty, which ruled in the region of Magadha in ancient India.
 
• He rose to prominence around the **5th century BCE**, succeeding the Shaishunaga dynasty and expanding the power of Magadha.
 
• Mahāpadma Nanda is often referred to as the "first empire builder" in Indian history due to his efforts to unite and expand territories across northern India.
 
• The Nanda dynasty centralized administration and strengthened its military, laying the foundation for future empires like the Maurya Empire.
 
• This period of Indian history is significant as it marked the transition to large-scale political entities and the beginning of organized imperial rule in the Indian subcontinent.
